proxy.label: Current proxy
proxy.directVpnUnused: not used in Direct VPN mode
proxy.directVpnIdle: Direct VPN mode, tunnel not running
proxy.externalTunnel: not needed: another VPN/TUN is already running
proxy.notSelected: proxies found, but none is selected (listeners: {{count}})

routes.label: Default and TUN routes
routes.viaTun: Internet traffic goes through our TUN
routes.notViaTun: the TUN runs, but the route to the Internet bypasses it

endpoint.notRun: not checked: curl.exe did not run

tunLog.label: Engine log
tunLog.historical: TUN stopped, these are past entries (errors: {{count}}); they say nothing about the current route

appLog.label: App log
appLog.problems: warnings and errors in the last 15 minutes: {{count}}

routing.tunnelOff: Protection is off — there is no routing to check.
routing.inconclusive: Could not measure both IPs (some echo servers did not answer). Run the check again.
routing.leak: The SAME IP ({{vpn}}) is seen through the VPN and directly. The tunnel does not change your public address — this is a leak, or the proxy goes direct.
routing.smartUnverified: The tunnel works (VPN {{vpn}} ≠ direct {{direct}}), but the Smart-RU runtime check did not finish: no reliable Russian echo through the TUN. Routing rules are covered by config tests; this live self-test only confirms the general VPN/direct split.
routing.smartOk: Everything works as intended: foreign sites go through the VPN ({{vpn}}) and Russian sites go direct with your real IP ({{direct}}). Smart RU mode really splits the traffic.
routing.ruViaVpn: The tunnel works, but the Russian host went out through the VPN ({{ru}}) instead of directly ({{direct}}). The Russian domain lists may still be downloading — try again in a minute.
routing.ok: The tunnel works: {{vpn}} is seen through the VPN, {{direct}} directly. Your public address really changes.
